target_clause: When using flow control, the receiver MUST read from the TCP receive buffer in a timely fashion.
next_clause: Failure to do so could lead to a deadlock when critical frames, such as WINDOW_UPDATE, are not read and acted upon.

previous_clause: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time, as they are returned immediately by clients.
target_clause: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames ([frame-new-token]) need to be valid for longer, but SHOULD NOT be accepted multiple times.
next_clause: Servers are encouraged to allow tokens to be used only once, if possible; tokens MAY include additional information about clients to further narrow applicability or reuse.

previous_clause: An endpoint detects a potential stateless reset when an incoming packet either cannot be associated with a connection, cannot be decrypted, or is marked as a duplicate packet.
target_clause: The endpoint MUST then compare the last 16 bytes of the packet with all Stateless Reset Tokens that are associated with connection IDs that the endpoint recently used to send packets from the IP address and port on which the datagram is received.
next_clause: This includes Stateless Reset Tokens from NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames and the server’s transport parameters.

previous_clause: Specifically, should the receiver drop packets that are received outside this window?
target_clause: Any truncated packet number received from a peer MUST be reconstructed as the value closest to the next expected packet number from that peer.
next_clause: (TODO: Clarify how packet number size can change mid-connection.)

previous_clause: A packet might be held in the OS kernel or elsewhere on the host before being processed.
target_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT include delays that it does not control when populating the Ack Delay field in an ACK frame.

previous_clause: This includes the initial and preferred_address transport parameter connection IDs.
target_clause: The peer SHOULD retire the corresponding connection IDs and send the corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames in a timely manner.
next_clause: The Retire Prior To field MUST be less than or equal to the Sequence Number field.

previous_clause: The sequence value can wrap; the value 65535 is followed by 0.
target_clause: When wrapping the sequence field, the server MUST ensure that a value with the same sequence has been received and acknowledged by the client.
next_clause: The connection ID that is assigned during the handshake is assumed to have a sequence of 65535.

previous_clause: If the PING frame is determined to be lost, a new PING frame SHOULD be generated.
target_clause: This PING frame MUST include a new Data field that is similarly difficult to guess.
next_clause: If validation of the new remote address fails, after allowing enough time for possible loss and recovery of packets carrying PING and PONG frames, the endpoint MUST terminate the connection.

target_clause: When a received protocol element is parsed, the recipient MUST be able to parse any value of reasonable length that is applicable to the recipient's role and that matches the grammar defined by the corresponding ABNF rules.
next_clause: Note, however, that some received protocol elements might not be parsed.

previous_clause: An endpoint MAY abandon address validation for an address that it considers to be already valid.
target_clause: That is, if successive connection migrations occur in quick succession with the final remote address being identical to the initial remote address, the endpoint MAY abandon address validation for that address.

previous_clause: In particular, an endpoint MAY choose to treat a stream error as a connection error.
target_clause: Endpoints SHOULD send a GOAWAY frame when ending a connection, providing that circumstances permit it.

previous_clause: Any received 0-RTT data that the server responds to might be due to a replay attack.
target_clause: Therefore, the server's use of 1-RTT keys MUST be limited to sending data before the handshake is complete.
next_clause: A server MUST NOT process incoming 1-RTT protected packets before the TLS handshake is complete.

previous_clause: If a server isn’t currently accepting any new connections, it SHOULD send an Initial packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with error code SERVER_BUSY.
target_clause: If the packet is a 0-RTT packet, the server MAY buffer a limited number of these packets in anticipation of a late-arriving Initial Packet.
next_clause: Clients are forbidden from sending Handshake packets prior to receiving a server response, so servers SHOULD ignore any such packets.

previous_clause: This allows implementations of Google QUIC to distinguish Google QUIC packets from short header packets sent by a client because Google QUIC servers expect the connection ID to always be present.
target_clause: The special interpretation of this bit SHOULD be removed from this specification when Google QUIC has finished transitioning to the new header format.
next_clause: Reserved:: The sixth, seventh, and eighth bits (0x7) of octet 0 are reserved for experimentation.

previous_clause: Upon receiving a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set, the sender of the altered settings can rely on the values from the oldest unacknowledged SETTINGS frame having been applied.
target_clause: If the sender of a SETTINGS frame does not receive an acknowledgment within a reasonable amount of time, it MAY issue a connection error of type SETTINGS_TIMEOUT.
next_clause: In setting a timeout, some allowance needs to be made for processing delays at the peer; a timeout that is solely based on the round trip time between endpoints might result in spurious errors.

previous_clause: Error codes of the format 0x1f * N + 0x21 for non-negative integer values of N are reserved to exercise the requirement that unknown error codes be treated as equivalent to H3_NO_ERROR ([extensions]).
target_clause: Implementations SHOULD select an error code from this space with some probability when they would have sent H3_NO_ERROR.

previous_clause: An endpoint MAY send data to an unvalidated peer address, but it MUST protect against potential attacks as described in [address-spoofing] and [on-path-spoofing].
target_clause: An endpoint MAY skip validation of a peer address if that address has been seen recently.
next_clause: In particular, if an endpoint returns to a previously-validated path after detecting some form of spurious migration, skipping address validation and restoring loss detection and congestion state can reduce the performance impact of the attack.

previous_clause: If a sender has sent data up to the limit, it will be unable to send new data and is considered blocked. A sender SHOULD send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate to the receiver that it has data to write but is blocked by flow control limits.
target_clause: If a sender is blocked for a period longer than the idle timeout ([idle-timeout]), the receiver might close the connection even when the sender has data that is available for transmission. To keep the connection from closing, a sender that is flow control limited SHOULD periodically send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame when it has no ack-eliciting packets in flight.

previous_clause: If verification fails, then the endpoint ceases setting ECT codepoints in subsequent packets with the expectation that either the network or the peer does not support ECN.
target_clause: If an endpoint sets ECT codepoints on outgoing packets and encounters a retransmission timeout due to the absence of acknowledgments from the peer (see [QUIC-RECOVERY]), or if an endpoint has reason to believe that a network element might be corrupting ECN codepoints, the endpoint MAY cease setting ECT codepoints in subsequent packets.
next_clause: Doing so allows the connection to traverse network elements that drop or corrupt ECN codepoints in the IP header.
